explain.curious: Tables give a reaction's energy at 25 °C. A vent at 90 °C or an ice-moon ocean near 0 °C changes it, sometimes enough to decide whether anything can live on it.
explain.science: Integrated Gibbs-Helmholtz equation with the reaction enthalpy held at its 298.15 K value. Good to a few kJ per mole across liquid-water temperatures; beyond about 150 °C the heat-capacity terms of the full revised HKF model matter (Amend and Shock 2001 tabulate those).

explain.curious: Whether a reaction can feed life depends on how much of each ingredient is actually there. Plenty of fuel and little waste makes it pay; a build-up of waste can shut it off.
explain.science: Free energy of reaction at the local activities. Negative means energy is released. Q is the product of activities raised to their stoichiometric coefficients (products positive, reactants negative); at pH 7 the hydrogen ion activity is 10^-7.
